publisher: Delhi High Court order dated 15 June 2024
statement: The purchase order for CONCOR's commercial software project defined ten milestones, including vendor testing, CONCOR testing, field-user deployment/testing, data migration and Go-live, and software acceptance/start of warranty.

publisher: Delhi High Court order dated 15 June 2024
statement: The petitioner relied on correspondence stating that software had been deployed for testing by field users and alleged that CONCOR had not provided sign-off for milestones 5 to 8.

publisher: Delhi High Court order dated 15 June 2024
statement: The respondent stated that the petitioner had failed to complete milestones 5 to 10 by 31 March 2024 even after revised timelines and had not completed any of the stipulated 48 cycles.

publisher: Delhi High Court order dated 15 June 2024
statement: The Court's earlier order declined to restrain termination and recorded a prima facie view that delays existed and that repeated extensions did not prevent CONCOR from exercising contractual rights to levy liquidated damages or terminate.

publisher: Delhi High Court order dated 15 June 2024
statement: CONCOR issued communication invoking the performance bank guarantee for Rs.35,40,000 after the termination dispute; the petitioner challenged the invocation and sought protection.

The Court dismissed the application and held that, after termination was not stayed, invocation of the performance bank guarantee followed contractually; the record did not establish fraud, irretrievable injustice, or special equity warranting interference.
